heroText: Lusaka is Zambia's plateau capital, a fast-growing commercial hub centred on the long, shop-lined Cairo Road. First-time visitors should browse crafts at Kabwata Cultural Village, learn Zambian history at the Lusaka National Museum, and pay respects at the Freedom Statue downtown. Kenneth Kaunda International Airport connects the city nationally and regionally, and Lusaka works well as a stopover before heading to Victoria Falls or South Luangwa's safari lodges.

areas.name: Cairo Road / City Centre
areas.text: Cairo Road and the surrounding city centre form Lusaka's main commercial strip, with shops, banks and markets within walking distance.

areas.name: Kabulonga
areas.text: Kabulonga is an upscale residential suburb of leafy streets, restaurants and some of Lusaka's better guesthouses.

areas.name: Woodlands
areas.text: Woodlands is a central residential area near malls and embassies, convenient for longer business stays.

areas.name: Rhodes Park
areas.text: Rhodes Park sits close to downtown offices and diplomatic missions, a practical base for short official visits.

airports.name: Kenneth Kaunda International Airport (LUN)
airports.search: Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, Lusaka, Zambia
airports.text: Kenneth Kaunda International Airport sits about 25 kilometres northeast of the city centre, with taxis and hotel shuttles covering the drive in.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Kenneth Kaunda International Airport (LUN) and central Lusaka before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base along Cairo Road for an easy first stay near shops, banks and the National Museum, or choose Kabulonga for quieter, upscale streets and dining. Woodlands and Rhodes Park suit business travelers wanting central offices and embassies within reach.
hotelIntro: Lusaka hotel choice depends on priorities: Cairo Road suits first-time visitors wanting central sights and shopping, Kabulonga suits longer, quieter stays with good restaurants, and Woodlands or Rhodes Park suit business and diplomatic visitors.
rentalCars: A rental car helps for day trips to nearby parks or onward travel toward Livingstone, though central Lusaka is easily covered by taxi or ride-hailing.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Lusaka base by repeat journeys: sights, evening food, station access and the airport transfer should all still work.

travelTips.title: Onward travel
travelTips.text: Use Lusaka as a stopover when connecting to Victoria Falls, South Luangwa or Lower Zambezi National Park.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Book a hotel shuttle or taxi from Kenneth Kaunda International Airport for the roughly 30-minute ride into the city.

travelTips.title: Craft shopping
travelTips.text: Visit Kabwata Cultural Village for Zambian wood carvings and baskets at fairer prices than tourist-area shops.

nearbyIdeas.name: Lower Zambezi National Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Wildlife
nearbyIdeas.text: Lower Zambezi National Park offers riverside safaris a few hours from Lusaka, known for elephants, hippos and canoe trips.

nearbyIdeas.name: Kalimba Reptile Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Wildlife
nearbyIdeas.text: Kalimba Reptile Park just outside Lusaka lets visitors see crocodiles and snakes up close, an easy half-day family outing.

nearbyIdeas.name: Victoria Falls
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Victoria Falls lies a flight or long drive southwest in Livingstone, one of Africa's most spectacular natural landmarks.

history.text: The section of line through Lusaka was built by the Mashonaland Railway Company, extending the line by 452 kilometres (281 mi) from Kalomo through to the mining town of Broken Hill (now Kabwe).

history.label: 6th century
history.text: The earliest evidence of settlement in the area around what is now the Lusaka area dates to the 6th century.

history.label: 19th century

Lusaka was founded in 1905 as a water stop on the route and was named after a Chief Lusaaka, the leader of a nearby Lenje village.
The capital was initially at Kalomo, being switched to Livingstone in 1907.
